book.name: The Tourney at Port Lessing
book.text: At Port Lessing, for Lady Day, Sir Olivier Umfray reached the last four before Sir Walter Wyvenhoe put him out. He broke 2 lances and bore Sir Thibaut Fenwick to the ground. He was himself borne down by Sir Walter Wyvenhoe. The prize went to Sir Everard Umfray. In the tourney in the field he took nobody. He was taken himself, by Sir Simon Stavely, and ransomed. His side carried the field. The prize of the tourney went to Sir Everard Umfray. The heralds wrote well of his conduct.

book.name: The Tourney at Merrow
book.text: At Merrow, for Eastertide, Sir Olivier Umfray rode in the first round and was put out by Sir Osbert Stavely. He broke 1 lance. The prize went to Sir Walter Wyvenhoe. In the tourney in the field he took nobody. He was taken himself, by Sir William Gournay, and ransomed. His side was beaten. The prize of the tourney went to Sir Walter Wyvenhoe.

book.name: The joust on the green at Merrow
book.text: At Merrow, for Whitsun, Sir Olivier Umfray carried the prize. He broke 6 lances and bore Sir Fulk de Brisac to the ground.

book.name: The joust on the green at Ambry Cross
book.text: At Ambry Cross, for Midsummer, Sir Olivier Umfray carried the prize. He broke 5 lances. He vowed to bear Sir Robert Sallow down, and did not. The heralds wrote that his conduct was wanting.

book.name: The joust of the mayor and aldermen at Port Lessing
book.text: At Port Lessing, for St James, Sir Olivier Umfray rode to the last two, and was beaten there by Sir Tristan Morrow. He broke 4 lances. The prize went to Sir Tristan Morrow.

book.name: The joust of the Guild of St Barbara at Saltings Quay
book.text: At Saltings Quay, for Lammas, Sir Olivier Umfray rode to the last two, and was beaten there by Sir Robert Ashcombe. He broke 4 lances. The prize went to Sir Robert Ashcombe.

book.name: The Tourney at Saltings Quay
book.text: At Saltings Quay, for Michaelmas, Sir Olivier Umfray rode in the first round and was put out by Sir Hugh Quarles. He broke no lance. The prize went to Sir Fulk de Brisac. In the tourney in the field he took Sir Simon Stavely prisoner. He was taken himself, by Sir Tristan Quarles, and ransomed. His side was beaten. The prize of the tourney went to Sir Jehan Challon.

book.name: The Tourney at Sallowfield
book.text: At Sallowfield, for St Luke, Sir Olivier Umfray reached the last four before Sir Osbert Stavely put him out. He broke 2 lances and struck the helm once. The prize went to Sir Edmund Sallow. In the tourney in the field he took nobody. He was taken himself, by Sir Robert Sallow, and ransomed. His side was beaten. The prize of the tourney went to Sir Hugh Westmere.

book.name: The joust on the green at Othery
book.text: At Othery, for Lady Day, Sir Olivier Umfray rode in the first round and was put out by Sir Tristan Morrow. He broke no lance. To his shame, his lance found a horse, and the heralds wrote that down too. The prize went to Sir Tristan Morrow. The heralds wrote that his conduct was wanting.

book.name: The Tourney at Othery
book.text: At Othery, for Whitsun, Sir Olivier Umfray rode in the first round and was put out by Sir Geoffrey de Vauclair. He broke 3 lances. The prize went to Sir Hugh Westmere. In the tourney in the field he took Sir Robert Sallow, Sir William Gournay and Sir Bertrand de Lisle prisoner. The two sides were judged even. The heralds gave him the prize of the tourney.

book.name: The joust on the green at Queenshythe
book.text: At Queenshythe, for Midsummer, Sir Olivier Umfray rode in the first round and was put out by Sir Tristan Pemberton. He broke no lance. He was himself borne down by Sir Tristan Pemberton. He was carried from the lists and the surgeon was sent for. The prize went to Sir Raoul Thorne. The heralds wrote well of his conduct.

book.name: The Earl of Stane’s Tourney
book.text: At Castle Brede, for Lammas, Sir Olivier Umfray rode in the first round and was put out by Sir Gilles Thorne. He broke 1 lance. The prize went to Sir Gilles Thorne. In the tourney in the field he took Sir Thibaut Fenwick prisoner. His side carried the field. The prize of the tourney went to Sir Olivier Westmere. At the barriers he beat Sir Everard Umfray and Sir Walter Wyvenhoe, and was given the prize of the axe.

book.name: The Tourney at Hollin Moor
book.text: At Hollin Moor, for Michaelmas, Sir Olivier Umfray carried the prize. He broke 8 lances and bore Sir Robert Ashcombe to the ground. In the tourney in the field he took Sir Louis Kerville and Sir Warin Brackmere prisoner. The two sides were judged even. The prize of the tourney went to Sir Everard de Rochemont.

book.name: The Tourney at Saltings Quay
book.text: At Saltings Quay, for St Luke, Sir Olivier Umfray rode in the first round and was put out by Sir Gilbert Westmere. He broke 1 lance. The prize went to Sir Fulk Darnay. In the tourney in the field he took Sir Robert Sallow prisoner. He was taken himself, by Sir Hugh Quarles, and ransomed. His side was beaten. The prize of the tourney went to Sir Hugh Quarles.

book.name: A vow broken
book.text: Sir Olivier Umfray vowed on the swans at Candlemas to break fifteen lances before the year is out. He did not keep it.

book.name: The Tourney at Saltings Quay
book.text: At Saltings Quay, for Lady Day, Sir Olivier Umfray rode in the first round and was put out by Sir Roger de Beaumaine. He broke 1 lance. The prize went to Sir Hugh Quarles. In the tourney in the field he took Sir Henry de Vauclair prisoner and beat Sir Bertrand Ashcombe from the saddle. His side was beaten. The prize of the tourney went to Sir Geoffrey de Brisac.

book.name: The Duke of Aumbry’s Tourney
book.text: At Ambry Cross, for Whitsun, Sir Olivier Umfray rode in the first round and was put out by Sir Olivier Westmere. He broke 1 lance and struck the helm once. He was himself borne down by Sir Olivier Westmere. The prize went to Sir Tristan Quarles. In the tourney in the field he took Sir Tristan Morrow and Sir Simon Kestrel prisoner. His side carried the field. The prize of the tourney went to Sir Everard Umfray. At the barriers he beat Sir Tristan Morrow and Sir Olivier Westmere, and was given the prize of the axe.

book.name: The Earl of Stane’s Tourney
book.text: At Castle Brede, for Lammas, Sir Olivier Umfray rode in the first round and was put out by Sir Everard Umfray. He broke no lance. He was himself borne down by Sir Everard Umfray. The prize went to Sir Everard Umfray. In the tourney in the field he took Sir Fulk de Brisac prisoner. His side carried the field. The prize of the tourney went to Sir Gilles Thorne. At the barriers he was beaten by Sir Geoffrey de Brisac. The prize of the axe went to Sir Arnaud Ingram.

book.name: The Tourney at Saltings Quay
book.text: At Saltings Quay, for Michaelmas, Sir Olivier Umfray reached the last four before Sir Humphrey Harrowby put him out. He broke 3 lances and bore Sir Tristan Morrow to the ground. book.name: The Tourney at Hollin Moor
book.text: At Hollin Moor, for Eastertide, Sir Olivier Umfray rode in the first round and was put out by Sir Piers Denholm. He broke 2 lances. He was himself borne down by Sir Piers Denholm. book.name: The Duke of Aumbry’s Tourney

book.name: The King’s Tourney at Midsummer
book.text: At Kingsmead, for Midsummer, Sir Olivier Umfray rode in the first round and was put out by Sir Olivier Westmere. He broke 1 lance and struck the helm once. The prize of the tourney went to Sir Humphrey Orme. At the barriers he was beaten by Sir Edmund Sallow. The prize of the axe went to Sir Humphrey Orme.

book.name: The Earl of Stane’s Tourney
book.text: At Castle Brede, for Lammas, Sir Olivier Umfray rode in the first round and was put out by Sir Walter Ingram. He broke 4 lances. The prize went to Sir Gilles Thorne. The prize of the axe went to Sir Nicholas de Brisac.

book.text: At Port Lessing, for Michaelmas, Sir Olivier Umfray reached the last four before Sir Geoffrey de Vauclair put him out. He broke 4 lances, struck the helm once and bore Sir Bertrand de Lisle to the ground. He was himself borne down by Sir Geoffrey de Vauclair. The heralds gave him the prize for the most helm strikes of the day. The prize went to Sir Simon Stavely. In the tourney in the field he took Sir Robert Ashcombe prisoner. He was taken himself, by Sir Tristan Morrow, and ransomed. His side was beaten. The prize of the tourney went to Sir Tristan Morrow.

book.name: The Tourney at Wystan’s Ford
book.text: At Wystan’s Ford, for Lady Day, Sir Olivier Umfray rode to the last two, and was beaten there by Sir Richard Kestrel. He broke 6 lances, struck the helm twice and bore Sir Geoffrey de Vauclair to the ground. The heralds gave him the prize for the most helm strikes of the day. The prize went to Sir Richard Kestrel. In the tourney in the field he took Sir Warin Brackmere and Sir Louis Marlowe prisoner. His side carried the field. The prize of the tourney went to Sir Jehan Challon.

book.name: The Tourney at Fennick
book.text: At Fennick, for Eastertide, Sir Olivier Umfray rode to the last two, and was beaten there by Sir Fulk Darnay. He broke 4 lances, struck the helm once and bore Sir Ralph Ashcombe to the ground. The heralds gave him the prize for the most helm strikes of the day. The prize went to Sir Fulk Darnay. In the tourney in the field he took Sir Arnaud Ingram prisoner and beat Sir Humphrey Harrowby and Sir Gilbert Westmere from the saddle. His side carried the field. The heralds gave him the prize of the tourney. It was thought a small field for a knight of his name.

lines: Sir Nicholas Sallow won the King’s Tourney at Midsummer.
Fire took the bowyers’ street at Sallowfield. The king sent timber; the bowyers sent him a bow.
Scarrow raiders burned three farms above Othery. The Earl’s men followed them to the hills and no farther, as the treaty requires.
The Princess Isabeau married Lord Geoffrey of Stane at Kingsmead. The Duke of Aumbry sent a silver ewer.
Sir Walter Ingram won the King’s Tourney at Midsummer.
Master Piers Cantle, King of Arms, finished a new roll of every coat of arms in Lothmere, and found three knights bearing arms they had no right to.
The harvest failed in the Saltings, and bread doubled in price at Merrow before Martinmas.
The Company of the Swan chose Sir Gilles Thorne to fill the stall of Sir Nicholas Sallow.
The Duke of Aumbry built a new gatehouse at Ambry Cross, facing the Kingsmead road.
Sir Everard Umfray won the King’s Tourney at Midsummer.
Sir Tristan Quarles, 2 times a champion, hung up his lance.
A ship of Port Lessing came home from Arle with a cargo of harness, a unicorn’s horn, and a sick crew. Only the harness was genuine.
The Guild of St Barbara cast a great bell for Port Lessing, named it Barbara, and hung it where every ship in the harbour could hear it.
Aumbry’s men and Stane’s fought with cudgels at the summer fair, the first blood between the houses since the war.
Sir Olivier Westmere won the King’s Tourney at Midsummer.
The king did not ride to hounds this year, for the first time anyone can remember.
A comet hung over the March for nine nights. The Earl of Stane’s astrologer said it meant nothing, which nobody believed.
The king fell at mass on Whitsunday. A council of regency rules in his name.
Sir Richard Kestrel won the King’s Tourney at Midsummer.
The Duke of Aumbry bought the wardship of three orphaned heirs of the March, and with it the use of their lands.
The canons of Fennick priory were given a relic of St Wystan’s finger, and the shrine at the ford denied he had ever lost one.
The great houses forbade their men to ride against each other at their own tourneys.
Sir Gilles Thorne won the King’s Tourney at Midsummer.
Stane and Aumbry both sent gifts to the Archbishop at Easter. The Archbishop sent both back.
The heralds of Kingsmead quarrelled with the heralds of Ambry Cross over whose roll was the true one. The King of Arms settled it by burning both.
